interpretation: The intended output is a 0–100 estimate that the Doom Thesis is the most likely medium-term regime. Until the indicator history is frozen and calibrated, it is a research-completion scorecard rather than a probability.
publication_rule: Do not publish a numeric score until at least 80% of proposed component weight has current, reproducible indicators and the historical calibration has been reviewed out of sample.

stop_rule.override: If the probability that U.S. productivity averages at least 5% for the next five years becomes the base case (50% or greater), cap the Doom Index at 19 even if other components remain elevated.
stop_rule.missing_warrant: A forecast ensemble and a market- or survey-implied probability for sustained 5% productivity growth do not yet exist. Realized productivity alone cannot establish the forward base case.

components.title: Fiscal constraint
components.contention: The United States has a structural fiscal gap that cannot be closed painlessly under consensus growth.
components.plain_english: Debt, interest, and promised-program funding are growing faster than the ordinary tax base. Stabilization requires unusually strong growth, materially higher revenue, benefit reform, inflation, or some combination.
components.score_rule: Score from debt and deficit trajectories, interest burden, program-gap annual equivalent, and the size of the recurring adjustment required to reach the prudent scenario.
components.update_frequency: Daily debt; monthly interest model; CBO vintage; annual Trustees reports
missing_warrants: Freeze a reproducible fiscal-stress normalization rather than scoring the size of liabilities by judgment.
Separate current-law arithmetic from claims that no politically plausible adjustment path exists.
Backtest how the proposed measures behaved before prior fiscal consolidations and inflation regimes.

claims.text: The current debt, interest, Social Security, and Medicare arithmetic is measured and sourced.
claims.note: The existing daily panel, Trustees estimates, CBO baseline, and security-level Treasury roll model support this.

claims.text: The prudent scenario requires a very large recurring adjustment under current assumptions.
claims.note: The page shows the deficit correction and program-gap funding separately to avoid double counting.

claims.text: Demographics make a wartime-sized debt ratio harder to stabilize than in 1945.
claims.note: The OASDI beneficiary-to-worker series and gross debt/GDP comparison are already present.

claims.text: There is no obvious path to balancing the budget.
claims.note: The arithmetic is supported; the word “path” requires political and behavioral evidence developed in the political-feasibility component.

components.title: Productivity escape
components.contention: Rapid productivity acceleration is not yet the base case, and the fiscal escape velocity is far above consensus.
components.plain_english: Ordinary productivity growth does not make the liability stack disappear. The thesis breaks only if AI produces a sustained, economy-wide step-change large enough to outrun the obligations.
components.score_rule: Combine realized nonfarm-business productivity, forecast distributions, output-per-dollar measures, and the probability of five-year productivity at or above 5%. Lower growth produces a higher Doom score.
components.update_frequency: Quarterly BLS; annual physical and human-capital panels; monthly forecast review
missing_warrants: Build a forecast ensemble for five-year productivity rather than equating one strong quarter with a regime change.
Estimate AI's positive and negative productivity channels without assuming the net sign.
Specify the exact probability estimator that activates the 5% stop-out override.

candidate_markets.label: Polymarket: U.S. GDP growth in 2026
candidate_markets.use: Near-term GDP proxy only; not a productivity or five-year market.

candidate_markets.label: Kalshi: quarterly U.S. GDP growth
candidate_markets.use: Near-term growth nowcast; not the thesis-breaking productivity probability.

candidate_markets.label: Polymarket: U.S. recession by end-2026
candidate_markets.use: Cyclical downside proxy, not structural productivity.

claims.text: Observed productivity has not yet established a sustained 5% regime.
claims.note: The existing BLS quarterly and five-year trend series supports the historical statement, not the forward probability.

claims.text: Several high-spending systems are producing weak measured output gains.
claims.note: Utilities and education are documented descriptively, but the charts do not establish causation.

claims.text: AI's offsetting effects will prevent massive net productivity acceleration.
claims.note: This is central to the thesis but currently has no decomposed empirical model.

claims.text: Five-percent sustained productivity growth would invalidate the Doom base case.
claims.note: The threshold is now explicit; the forecast-probability mechanism is not yet built.

components.title: AI capital intensity and returns
components.contention: AI requires massive capital investment whose realized economic return remains uncertain.
components.plain_english: The buildout can add to GDP while still destroying capital if revenue, margins, and durable cash flow do not compensate for data-center, power, networking, and model costs.
components.score_rule: Track hyperscaler AI capex, incremental AI revenue and gross profit, depreciation, power demand, data-center utilization, and an estimated incremental return on invested capital.
components.update_frequency: Quarterly filings and earnings calls; monthly infrastructure and pricing checks
missing_warrants: Create a point-in-time hyperscaler capex and AI-revenue panel with consistent company definitions.
Separate replacement capex, ordinary cloud capex, and genuinely incremental AI infrastructure.
Estimate incremental ROIC under low, base, and high monetization cases.
Track the memory bottleneck with HBM supply, price, lead-time, and accelerator-utilization data.

claims.text: AI capital expenditure is massive relative to its directly attributable cash return.
claims.note: The current Doom page has no AI-specific capex or monetization dataset.

claims.text: The economic return on the AI buildout is questionable.
claims.note: This needs an explicit counterfactual and incremental-return model, not anecdotes.

claims.text: A memory-enterprise bottleneck has delayed the full social and economic impact.
claims.note: No HBM capacity, pricing, lead-time, or compute-utilization series is present.

claims.text: The cost of generating AI video is falling rapidly.
claims.note: A reproducible quality-adjusted dollars-per-second benchmark does not yet exist.

components.title: The distraction economy
components.contention: AI may raise measured capability while reducing human attention, agency, and effective productivity through personalized media and addiction loops.
components.plain_english: Cheaper, more personalized content can consume the time and focus that better tools theoretically save. A productivity model that counts only workplace automation misses this offset.
components.score_rule: Measure attention-platform value and usage against industrial capacity, screen-time intensity, ad-personalization economics, labor displacement, and credible causal estimates of attention loss.
components.update_frequency: Quarterly market-cap and revenue panel; annual time-use data; research-vintage updates
missing_warrants: Define and publish the AAPL/GOOGL/META/NFLX and related screen-time basket versus a U.S. industrial basket.
Add time-use and platform-engagement series without treating market capitalization as proof of social harm.
Quantify the incremental revenue and engagement effects of recommendation and personalization systems.
Identify a defensible causal bridge from attention capture to economy-wide productivity.

claims.text: The primary economy is increasingly a distraction economy.
claims.note: The category is not yet operationally defined.

claims.text: Screen-time platform value has outgrown U.S. industrial market value.
claims.note: The requested basket comparison has not yet been constructed.

claims.text: AI personalization materially increases media and advertising consumption.
claims.note: Company disclosures and external experiments must be assembled.

claims.text: The resulting attention loss offsets a meaningful share of AI productivity gains.
claims.note: This needs causal evidence and sensitivity bounds.

components.title: Political feasibility of adjustment
components.contention: The austerity and revenue package required by the fiscal arithmetic is politically infeasible before crisis conditions.
components.plain_english: The arithmetic can identify a bill; it cannot prove Congress will pay it. This component asks whether voters and institutions will accept the required taxes, spending restraint, or benefit changes before markets force the issue.
components.score_rule: Combine legislative prediction markets, fiscal-policy polling, roll-call behavior, enacted primary-balance changes, and independent budget scores. Lower probability of timely adjustment produces a higher score.
components.update_frequency: Weekly market/poll review; event-driven legislation; quarterly policy score

candidate_markets.label: Kalshi: Congress and legislation
candidate_markets.use: Useful for bill passage and shutdown proxies; no direct prudent-fiscal-package contract found.

candidate_markets.label: Polymarket: peak U.S. national debt before 2027
candidate_markets.use: Debt-path proxy with limited horizon and liquidity.

candidate_markets.label: Kalshi: crypto market-structure legislation
candidate_markets.use: Legislative-capacity and financialization proxy, not an austerity probability.

missing_warrants: No liquid market directly prices passage of a package comparable to the prudent reduction scenario.
Build a historical fiscal-legislation database and define what counts as decisive adjustment.
Add public-opinion support for taxes, benefits, spending cuts, inflation tolerance, and financial repression.
Model revenue feedback and policy dilution between proposal and enactment.

claims.text: A prudent fiscal adjustment is politically infeasible under current conditions.
claims.note: The current page quantifies cost, not passage probability.

claims.text: Prediction markets can provide useful political and macro inputs.
claims.note: Relevant GDP, debt, shutdown, and legislation markets exist, but none directly resolves the core fiscal package.

claims.text: Politicians will choose indirect adjustment before explicit austerity.
claims.note: This requires historical base rates and observable policy probabilities.

components.title: Debasement and financial repression
components.contention: If explicit adjustment fails, policymakers will lean on inflation, money creation, captive demand, and digital financial control.
components.plain_english: The bill can be paid visibly through taxes and cuts or less visibly through lower real returns on money and bonds. Digital rails may increase the state's ability to target, monitor, or restrict that adjustment—but that outcome is not automatic.
components.score_rule: Track inflation expectations, term premium and rate volatility, central-bank balance sheets, real yields, Treasury ownership, regulatory captive-demand measures, and concrete U.S. digital-money policy milestones.
components.update_frequency: Daily markets; monthly balance sheets; event-driven legislation and regulation
missing_warrants: Add breakeven inflation, inflation swaps, term premium, MOVE, real yields, and central-bank balance-sheet history.
Define financial repression with observable policy triggers rather than using it as a catch-all label.
Track actual U.S. CBDC, stablecoin, bank-reserve, and programmable-money legislation separately.
Distinguish wealth taxation, capital controls, and asset confiscation; they are not interchangeable.

claims.text: Fiscal pressure increases incentives for inflationary or repressive adjustment.
claims.note: The incentive is plausible and historically grounded, but the current page lacks a regime model.

claims.text: CBDCs or digitized money will be used for wealth taxation and control.
claims.note: No current U.S. policy path or conditional probability is supplied.

claims.text: Inflation expectations will unanchor and fixed-income volatility will force repression.
claims.note: The relevant market series and thresholds are absent.

claims.text: Asset confiscation is a likely endpoint.
claims.note: The term requires a precise legal and economic definition before it can enter the score.

components.title: Institutional legitimacy and control
components.contention: Declining legitimacy and rising distributional conflict increase the risk of authoritarian, command-and-control responses.
components.plain_english: When the fiscal bargain loses legitimacy, compliance becomes harder and coercion becomes more attractive. Trust and administrative leakage are measurable; the path from those facts to authoritarianism is not yet established.
components.score_rule: Use trust, democratic-governance, protest and unrest, corruption, improper-payment, executive-power, surveillance, and civil-liberty indicators with predeclared thresholds.
components.update_frequency: Annual institutional datasets; quarterly polling; event-driven legal and security review
missing_warrants: Add long-run trust and democratic-governance series with clear U.S. comparability.
Separate improper payments, fraud, corruption, and low trust; one does not prove another.
Define and track unrest, executive-power expansion, surveillance, and asset-control events.
Estimate transition probabilities rather than narrating an inevitable authoritarian sequence.

claims.text: Trust in the federal government is low by the existing series.
claims.note: The page reports the Pew history and latest level.

claims.text: Administrative leakage is relevant to institutional capacity.
claims.note: CMS improper payments are measured, but CMS explicitly says they are not a fraud estimate.

claims.text: Social unrest and democratic dissatisfaction are accelerating toward authoritarian government.
claims.note: The page has no unrest, democracy, civil-liberty, or executive-power panel.

claims.text: AI will be used to suppress dissent and solidify command-and-control rule.
claims.note: This is a scenario requiring signposts, not a warranted current-state claim.

downstream_scenarios.title: Financial bread and circuses
downstream_scenarios.summary: Legalized gambling, prediction markets, tokenized equities, perpetual swaps, and stablecoin collateral become politically useful outlets and financial rails.
downstream_scenarios.needed: Stablecoin supply and velocity, gambling and prediction-market handle, perpetual volume, tokenized-asset issuance, legislation, and a causal mechanism connecting these to fiscal policy.

downstream_scenarios.title: Temporary command-and-control economy
downstream_scenarios.summary: AI-enabled surveillance, military capacity, and centralized financial rails strengthen human authoritarian control during the adjustment phase.
downstream_scenarios.needed: Operational definitions, policy signposts, procurement and surveillance data, legal authorities, and historical transition rates.

downstream_scenarios.title: Exit from Doom through superintelligence
downstream_scenarios.summary: Superintelligence eventually supersedes the human command structure and may generate an abundance or governance regime that invalidates the fiscal frame.
downstream_scenarios.needed: Treat as a path-dependent scenario rather than a scored fact. The cited Elon Musk control claim needs a primary transcript and should remain non-scoring.

strategy_modules.title: Macro: hard assets versus fiat
strategy_modules.thesis: Own scarce real assets and short structurally weak fiat currencies when debasement and repression signals rise.
strategy_modules.requirements: Define the asset and currency universe, valuation filter, carry, trend, entry/exit rules, transaction costs, sizing, and historical drawdown test.

strategy_modules.title: Long/short Doom equities
strategy_modules.thesis: Rank companies by alignment with fiscal transfer, scarcity, command-and-control, attention, and capital-intensity regimes.
strategy_modules.requirements: Create a point-in-time stock taxonomy, auditable features, neutralization rules, valuation support, filing-event signals, and a survivorship-safe backtest.

strategy_modules.title: Tactical and on-chain perennials
strategy_modules.thesis: Trade liquid perps and tokenized markets around intra-quarter changes in the Doom components.
strategy_modules.requirements: Specify venues, collateral, liquidation and oracle risks, funding costs, market-impact assumptions, custody constraints, and hard risk limits before any performance claim.

strategy_modules.title: Index stop and portfolio governor
strategy_modules.thesis: Exit Doom-linked risk when the index falls below 20 or the productivity override activates.
strategy_modules.requirements: The rule is explicit; it still needs a published daily score, revision policy, execution convention, slippage model, and test for threshold whipsaw.
